# Multi-tenant SaaS

Applies when the change touches: code that reads or writes data belonging to a tenant, organization, workspace, or customer account in a shared deployment. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization, applied across tenants | 2023, second edition | 2026-09-28 | <https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/> |
| Tenant isolation (AWS Well-Architected SaaS Lens) | living lens document | 2026-09-28 | <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/saas-lens/tenant-isolation.html> |
| PostgreSQL row security policies as a second layer of tenant isolation | PostgreSQL 18, section 5.9 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Name every table, bucket, cache key, queue, and search index the change touches that holds tenant data; a new one without a tenant key is a design question before Specify. |
| Specify | Acceptance states that a client of tenant B cannot read, list, update, or delete tenant A's data through each changed operation, and names the expected response (404, not 403, where existence must not leak). |
| Specify | Every cross-tenant query (billing roll-ups, support tools, analytics) is named in the Spec, runs under a separate role or service, and is unreachable from customer-facing endpoints. |
| Implement | The tenant id comes only from the authenticated token or session, never from the request body, the query string, a path parameter, or a header the client sets. |
| Implement | Tenant scoping lives in the data-access layer through a base query or repository every read and write goes through; a check after fetching the row is a finding, not a control. |
| Implement | Every joined or sub-queried table is filtered by the tenant id again; cache keys, object-storage paths, and search queries carry the tenant id too. |
| Implement | Row-level security (or the database's equivalent) enforces the same scoping as a second layer, with the application connecting under a role that cannot bypass it. |
| Review | Trace each changed query to its tenant filter; any raw query, bulk job, or new join without one, and any tenant id read from client input, is a finding. |
| Ship | Cross-tenant access denials and any query that runs without a tenant context are logged and alerted on during the observe window. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-tenant read test per data-access method | client B cannot see, list, or change client A's records through any repository method or endpoint the change touches | a parameterized test that seeds two tenants and calls every data-access method and endpoint as tenant B against tenant A's ids, in the repository suite |
| Tenant id from client input is ignored | a tenant id placed in the body, query, path, or a header does not change which tenant's data is returned | API tests that send tenant A's id in each position with tenant B's token and assert tenant B's scope |
| Row-level security enforced | the database refuses cross-tenant rows even when the application filter is missing | a test that connects as the application role, sets tenant A's context, and runs an unfiltered `SELECT` on each tenant table expecting only A's rows; `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` checked in a migration test |
| Unscoped query lint (emerging) | no query on a tenant table bypasses the scoped base query | a Semgrep rule (or the ORM's own check) that flags raw queries and direct model access on tenant tables outside the data-access layer |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
